quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road surface that has not washed away yet. Drive with extra caution during the first rain.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before turning left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This way, if another car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The road center has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a broken line in the center, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: Bad weather makes it hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther back from the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: In poor visibility, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop if danger appears.

questions.question: When can you block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection is illegal and you can get a ticket.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is only allowed from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is only allowed from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a dashed line, only the traffic next to the dashed line can pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the engine?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt and checking that all passengers have buckled theirs before starting the engine.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. Stop before the crosswalk if there is no stop line. Stop before the intersection if there is no crosswalk. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too dense to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?

options.text: Only if you are involved in a collision.
If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer when stopped for a traffic violation or after a collision.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition to prevent hydroplaning. If you lose control, release the gas pedal, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning when it rains?

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: Lower your speed in rainy weather to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes your tires to float on water instead of gripping the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines are the same for violations in work zones as for normal traffic violations.
You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
Slow down only if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to slow down or stop for equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: What is the correct way to back up?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not rely only on your mirrors, as they do not show the area directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you at night with high beams on. You cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What should a driver do if pedestrians are in an upcoming crosswalk?

options.text: Continue ahead. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are next to each other, you can only pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. High beams can blind the driver ahead. Only use high beams in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived first.
Across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also want to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This is very dangerous. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Pay close attention to workers and equipment.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May finish its turn in either lane.
May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: Long trucks need extra space to turn because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than their front wheels. They often swing wide to complete a right turn safely.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles
Where signs and road markings allow passing
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, curves, or hills. Only pass where signs and markings permit it and when you have enough safe space to complete the pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or school crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: You see animals standing near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive with caution. Animals may run or change direction suddenly. They also may travel in groups, so more animals could be near the road that you cannot see.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your way. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to not block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road, but a vehicle is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
Keep the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn so the pedestrian moves over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means traffic beside the broken line may pass. Traffic beside the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: When driving at night on a poorly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area your headlights show.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area your headlights show.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You are parked at a curb and want to enter traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to speed up and match the traffic flow.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, only return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.
